The OpenTofu GitHub repository has roughly 30.2k stars (about 30,200), measured 2026-09-21.
By GitHub stars, Kubernetes leads the broader infrastructure ecosystem, and among dedicated IaC tools Terraform is the most-starred, followed in order by OpenTofu, Pulumi, AWS CDK, and Crossplane.

Terraform's larger community reflects a decade of first-mover adoption, while Pulumi, OpenTofu, and Crossplane have grown fastest among teams prioritizing general-purpose languages, open governance, or Kubernetes-native infrastructure management, respectively.
Kubernetes is the de facto container orchestration standard.
The pricing table reflects published pricing as of September 2026.
env0 has been renamed to 'env zero' (env zero is formerly env0).
Spacelift's paid plans scale by private worker count rather than by seats or resources, with quote-based pricing at the top end.
env zero prices its paid tiers per successful apply or environment.
Spacelift and env zero are managed CI/CD layers frequently compared against the core IaC tools.
Pulumi Cloud's Free edition is free forever for one user, with unlimited stacks and projects and 500 workflow minutes per month.
Pulumi Cloud's Essentials plan starts at $40/month, including 40 credits and up to 500 managed resources.
Pulumi Cloud's Pro plan starts at $400/month, including 400 credits and up to 2,000 managed resources.
Pulumi Cloud's Enterprise plan is custom, contract-priced.
HCP Terraform is free for up to 500 managed resources with one concurrent run, then moves to per-resource pricing of roughly $0.10 to $0.99 per resource per month depending on tier.
Self-hosted Terraform Enterprise is available at custom pricing for larger organizations.
The managed-platform pricing figures (Pulumi Cloud, HCP Terraform) reflect published pricing checked on 2026-09-21.
Google Cloud Deployment Manager reached end of support on March 31, 2026.

claims.text: Google Cloud Infrastructure Manager replaces Google Cloud Deployment Manager and automates deployment and management of Google Cloud resources using Terraform configurations.

Governance and license table: Pulumi is Apache-2.0 under Pulumi Corporation; Terraform is BUSL-1.1 (not OSI-approved) under HashiCorp (an IBM company); AWS CDK is Apache-2.0 under AWS; Azure Bicep is MIT under Microsoft; Kubernetes and Crossplane are Apache-2.0 under the CNCF; OpenTofu is MPL-2.0 under the Linux Foundation.

The at-a-glance table states: Pulumi supports Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, .NET, Java, YAML, or HCL and is Apache-2.0; Terraform uses HCL and is BUSL-1.1; AWS CDK supports TypeScript, Python, Java, C#, Go, compiles to CloudFormation, is AWS-only and Apache-2.0; Kubernetes YAML is Apache-2.0.
AWS CloudFormation, Azure ARM, and Google Cloud Infrastructure Manager are proprietary managed services that are continuously updated by their respective vendors.
